## 1. Battery Storage & Power Electronics Governing Equations

### 1.1 Peukert's Law for Battery Discharge Duration
For lead-acid chemistries (AGM, Gel, Flooded), usable discharge capacity degrades non-linearly at elevated discharge C-rates. The runtime $t$ (hours) under constant discharge current $I$ (Amps) is modeled as:

```latex
t = H \cdot \left( \frac{C}{I \cdot H} \right)^k
```

Where:
- $t$: Battery runtime duration in hours
- $H$: Rated discharge time baseline in hours (typically $H = 20\text{ hours}$ for C20 lead-acid capacity ratings)
- $C$: Manufacturer rated Amp-hour capacity at baseline $H$ (Ah)
- $I$: Actual continuous discharge current in Amps ($I = P_{\text{load}} / (V_{\text{nominal}} \cdot \eta_{\text{inv}})$)
- $k$: Peukert exponent (dimensionless):
  - Flooded Lead-Acid: $k \approx 1.20 - 1.25$
  - AGM / Gel: $k \approx 1.10 - 1.15$
  - Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4): $k \approx 1.01 - 1.05$ (nearly linear, negligible Peukert loss)

### 1.2 Lithium Battery Usable Energy & DC-AC Inverter Dissipation
For modern Lithium-ion / LiFePO4 battery banks:

```latex
E_{\text{usable}} = C_{\text{rated}} \cdot V_{\text{nominal}} \cdot \text{DoD}_{\text{max}} \cdot \eta_{\text{temp}}
```

```latex
t_{\text{runtime}} = \frac{E_{\text{usable}} \cdot \eta_{\text{inverter}}}{P_{\text{continuous}} + P_{\text{tare}}}
```

Where:
- $\text{DoD}_{\text{max}}$: Recommended maximum Depth of Discharge ($0.80 - 0.90$ for LiFePO4, $0.50$ for Lead-Acid)
- $\eta_{\text{temp}}$: Thermal derating multiplier ($1.00$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$; drops to $0.80$ at $0^\circ\text{C}$)
- $\eta_{\text{inverter}}$: Inverter conversion efficiency under load ($0.90 - 0.96$)
- $P_{\text{tare}}$: Inverter idle / no-load standby power dissipation ($15\text{W} - 60\text{W}$)

---

## 2. Solar Photovoltaic Sizing & Irradiance Transposition

### 2.1 Daily & Annual AC Energy Production (NREL PVWatts V8 Model)
Daily AC solar energy output $E_{\text{daily}}$ (kWh/day) is derived from regional Peak Sun Hours (PSH) and comprehensive system derating:

```latex
E_{\text{daily}} = P_{\text{dc,STC}} \cdot \text{PSH} \cdot \eta_{\text{system}} \cdot \left[ 1 + \gamma_{Pmp} \cdot (T_{\text{cell}} - 25^\circ\text{C}) \right]
```

Where:
- $P_{\text{dc,STC}}$: DC nameplate array capacity in kilowatts (kW) under Standard Test Conditions ($1,000\text{ W/m}^2$, $25^\circ\text{C}$, AM 1.5G)
- $\text{PSH}$: Peak Sun Hours (equivalent hours per day at $1,000\text{ W/m}^2$ irradiance)
- $\eta_{\text{system}}$: Combined sub-system derate factor ($0.82 - 0.86$ typical), compounding:
  - Soiling loss: $2\% - 5\%$
  - Shading loss: $1\% - 3\%$
  - Wiring DC resistance: $1.5\% - 2\%$
  - Inverter AC conversion: $2.5\% - 4\%$
  - Module manufacturing mismatch: $1\% - 2\%$
- $\gamma_{Pmp}$: Temperature coefficient of maximum power (typically $-0.35\%/^\circ\text{C}$ for monocrystalline silicon)
- $T_{\text{cell}}$: Operating cell temperature ($T_{\text{cell}} = T_{\text{ambient}} + \text{PSH} \cdot \frac{\text{NOCT} - 20}{0.8}$)

### 2.2 Solar Array Sizing to Offset Target Consumption

```latex
P_{\text{dc,required}} = \frac{E_{\text{target,daily}}}{\text{PSH} \cdot \eta_{\text{system}}}
```

```latex
N_{\text{modules}} = \left\lceil \frac{P_{\text{dc,required}} \cdot 1000}{P_{\text{module,wattage}}} \right\rceil
```

### 2.3 Solar Charge Controller Headroom & Cold-Weather Voc (NEC 690.7)
Under sub-freezing conditions, photovoltaic open-circuit voltage ($V_{oc}$) increases significantly. Sizing requires the lowest expected ambient temperature $T_{\text{min}}$:

```latex
V_{oc,\text{max}} = V_{oc,\text{STC}} \cdot \left[ 1 + \beta_{Voc} \cdot (T_{\text{min}} - 25^\circ\text{C}) \right] \cdot N_{\text{series}}
```

Where:
- $\beta_{Voc}$: Temperature coefficient of $V_{oc}$ (typically $-0.28\%/^\circ\text{C}$ to $-0.30\%/^\circ\text{C}$)
- Charge controller maximum input rating $V_{\text{controller,max}}$ must satisfy: $V_{\text{controller,max}} \ge V_{oc,\text{max}}$

---

## 3. Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging & Electrical Infrastructure

### 3.1 Continuous Load 125% Rule for EV Branch Circuits (NEC 625.42 & 210.19)
Because EV charging operates continuously for 3 or more hours, the National Electrical Code classifies EVSE branch circuits as continuous loads:

```latex
I_{\text{breaker,min}} = I_{\text{continuous,charging}} \times 1.25
```

```latex
I_{\text{max,charging}} = I_{\text{breaker,rating}} \times 0.80
```

Standard North American Breaker & Charging Allocations:
- 15A Breaker $\rightarrow$ 12A continuous charging ($1.44\text{ kW}$ at 120V Level 1)
- 20A Breaker $\rightarrow$ 16A continuous charging ($3.84\text{ kW}$ at 240V Level 2)
- 40A Breaker $\rightarrow$ 32A continuous charging ($7.68\text{ kW}$ at 240V Level 2)
- 50A Breaker $\rightarrow$ 40A continuous charging ($9.60\text{ kW}$ at 240V Level 2)
- 60A Breaker $\rightarrow$ 48A continuous charging ($11.52\text{ kW}$ at 240V Level 2)
- 100A Breaker $\rightarrow$ 80A continuous charging ($19.20\text{ kW}$ at 240V Level 2)

### 3.2 AC-to-DC Charging Time Simulation with Taper Profile
Total charging energy required:

```latex
E_{\text{grid,input}} = \frac{\Delta \text{SoC} \cdot C_{\text{battery,usable}}}{\eta_{\text{onboard\_charger}} \cdot \eta_{\text{battery\_acceptance}}}
```

```latex
t_{\text{charge}} = \frac{E_{\text{grid,input}}}{P_{\text{EVSE,delivered}}}
```

Where:
- $\eta_{\text{onboard\_charger}}$: Onboard AC-to-DC rectification efficiency ($82\% - 86\%$ on 120V Level 1 due to continuous thermal/control overhead; $90\% - 94\%$ on 240V Level 2)
- $\Delta \text{SoC}$: State of Charge increase fraction (e.g., $0.20 \rightarrow 0.80 = 0.60$)

---

## 4. Heating, Ventilation & Air Conditioning (HVAC) Thermodynamics

### 4.1 Heat Pump Coefficient of Performance (COP) & SEER2 / HSPF2 Conversions
Seasonal energy efficiency metrics relate directly to instantaneous thermodynamic COP:

```latex
\text{COP}_{\text{cooling}} = \text{EER} \times 0.293071
```

```latex
\text{COP}_{\text{heating,seasonal}} = \text{HSPF2} \times 0.293071
```

Electrical power draw $\dot{W}_{\text{elec}}$ (kW) for delivered thermal capacity $\dot{Q}_{\text{thermal}}$ (BTU/hr):

```latex
\dot{W}_{\text{elec}} = \frac{\dot{Q}_{\text{thermal}}}{3412.142 \cdot \text{COP}(T_{\text{ambient}})}
```

### 4.2 ASHRAE Temperature Bin Method for Cold-Climate ccASHP
Seasonal operating cost over annual temperature bins $j = 1 \dots N$:

```latex
E_{\text{seasonal,kWh}} = \sum_{j=1}^{N} \left[ \frac{\dot{Q}_{\text{building}}(T_j)}{\text{COP}(T_j) \cdot 3412.142} \cdot n_j \right] + E_{\text{aux,resistive}}
```

Where:
- $n_j$: Number of annual hours in temperature bin $T_j$
- $\dot{Q}_{\text{building}}(T_j) = \text{UA}_{\text{envelope}} \cdot (T_{\text{indoor}} - T_j)$
- $E_{\text{aux,resistive}}$: Supplemental electric resistance strip heat required when outdoor temperature falls below the building's thermal balance point ($T_{\\text{ambient}} < T_{\\text{balance}}$)

---

## 5. Generator Sizing & Inductive Motor Inrush (NEC Article 430)

### 5.1 Motor Locked-Rotor Starting Inrush kVA
Inductive electric motors (air conditioner compressors, well pumps, sump pumps) draw $4\times - 7\times$ their running wattage during initial rotor acceleration. Inrush kVA is governed by NEMA Code Letters (NEC Table 430.7(B)):

```latex
\text{kVA}_{\text{starting}} = \frac{\text{HP} \cdot \text{kVA/HP}_{\text{Code Letter}}}{\eta_{\text{motor}}}
```

```latex
I_{\text{LRA}} = \frac{\text{kVA}_{\text{starting}} \cdot 1000}{V_{\text{line}} \cdot \sqrt{\phi}}
```

### 5.2 Generator Capacity Allocation

```latex
P_{\text{gen,continuous}} \ge \sum P_{\text{running,all}}
```

```latex
P_{\text{gen,surge}} \ge \sum P_{\text{running,non-motor}} + P_{\text{running,other-motors}} + P_{\text{starting,largest-motor}}
```

---

## 6. Conductor Voltage Drop (Ohm's Law & NEC 210.19(A))

Percentage voltage drop $VD_{\%}$ across single-phase AC circuits:

```latex
VD_{\text{volts}} = \frac{2 \cdot K \cdot I \cdot L}{A_{\text{cmil}}}
```

```latex
VD_{\%} = \left( \frac{VD_{\text{volts}}}{V_{\text{nominal}}} \right) \times 100\%
```

Where:
- $K$: Specific resistivity of conductor ($12.9\text{ }\Omega\cdot\text{cmil/ft}$ for Copper, $21.2\text{ }\Omega\cdot\text{cmil/ft}$ for Aluminum at $75^\circ\text{C}$)
- $I$: Load current in Amperes
- $L$: One-way circuit length in feet
- $A_{\text{cmil}}$: Conductor cross-sectional area in circular mils (from NEC Chapter 9 Table 8)
- NEC Recommendation: $VD_{\%} \le 3.0\%$ on branch circuits, $VD_{\%} \le 5.0\%$ total combined feeder + branch.

| SEER2 / HSPF2 to COP Factor | - | 0.293071 | W/BTU/hr | AHRI 210/240 |
